name: Provide Trade Studies
text: Trade studies shall be made available for review when requested or provided in accordance with the contract provisions.

name: Selection and Control of Parts, Materials, and Processes
text: Unless otherwise specified in the contract, the parts, materials, and processes shall be selected and controlled in accordance with contractor established and documented procedures to satisfy the requirements specified herein.

name: Quality and Reliability Emphasis
text: The selection and control procedures shall emphasize quality and reliability to meet the mission requirements and to minimize total life cycle costs for the applicable system.

name: Electronic Parts Standards
text: Electronic parts shall be JAN Class S or in accordance with MIL-STD-1547.

name: Commonality of Parts, Materials, and Processes
text: An additional objective in the selection of parts, materials, and processes shall be to maximize commonality and thereby minimize the variety of parts, related tools, and test equipment required in the fabrication, installation, and maintenance of the vehicle.

name: Prevention of Inadvertent Interchange
text: Identical electrical connectors, identical fluid fittings, or other identical parts shall not be used on a vehicle where inadvertent interchange of the items or interconnections could cause possible malfunction.

name: Proven Quality for Environmental Durability
text: The parts, materials, and processes selected shall be of sufficient proven quality to allow the space equipment to meet the functional performance, reliability, lifecycle, and strength requirements including all environmental degradation effects.

name: Resistance to Space Environment Damage
text: Parts, materials, and processes shall be selected to ensure that any damage or deterioration from the space environment, or the outgassing effects in the space environment, will not reduce the performance of the vehicle beyond the specified limits.

name: Selection of Suitable Materials
text: Materials shall, where practicable, be selected that have demonstrated their suitability for the intended application.

name: Use of Fungus-Inert Materials
text: Inherently fungus-inert materials shall be used, where practicable.

name: Restriction on Combustible or Toxic Materials
text: Combustible materials or materials that can generate toxic outgassing or toxic products of combustion shall not be used if cost-effective alternatives exist.

name: Low Outgassing Materials
text: Materials shall, where practicable, be selected for low outgassing in accordance with SP-R-0022 (NASA JSC).

name: Outgassing Performance Limits
text: The total mass loss in 24 hours shall be less than 1 percent, and the collected volatile condensable material shall be less than 0.1 percent when heated in vacuum (0.0001 Torr) to 125 deg C and collected at 23 deg C.

name: Analytical Contamination Modeling
text: Analytical contamination models shall be used to evaluate performance impacts of outgassing on adjacent critical equipment.

name: Swelling and Shrinkage Tolerances
text: Swelling and shrinkage characteristics of materials shall be shown to be within acceptable tolerances under worst case humidity and temperature cycling.

name: Corrosion Resistance of Metals
text: Metals shall be corrosion resistant, or shall be suitably treated to resist corrosion when subjected to the specified environments.

name: Protection of Dissimilar Metals
text: Protection of dissimilar metal combinations shall be in accordance with MIL-STD-889.

name: Avoidance of Stress Corrosion and Embrittlement
text: Care shall be exercised in the selection of materials and processes in accordance with MSFC-SPEC-522 and MIL-STD-1568 to avoid stress corrosion cracking, brittle fracture, and hydrogen embrittlement.

name: Restrictions on Certain Aluminum Alloys
text: Aluminum alloys 2020-T6, 7079-T6, and 7178-T6 shall not be used for structural applications. Use of 7075-T6, 2024-T3, 2024-T4, and 2014-T6 sheet material less than 6.3 mm thick is allowed if stresses are below acceptable limits and corrosion protection is provided.

name: Heat Treatment Requirements for 7075 Alloy
text: Other forms of 7075 shall be heat treated to the -T73 or -T76 temper.

name: Temperature Restrictions for Certain Alloys
text: The following alloys and heat treatments shall not be used above 65 deg C: 5083-H32, 5083-H38, 5086-H34, 5086-H38, 5456-H32, and 5456-H38.

name: Heat Treatment of Aluminum Parts
text: Heat treatment of aluminum alloy parts shall be in accordance with MIL-H-6088.

name: Heat Treatment of Steel Parts
text: Heat treatment of steel parts shall be in accordance with MIL-H-6875.

name: Heat Treatment of Titanium Parts
text: Heat treatment of titanium and titanium alloys shall be in accordance with MIL-H-81200.

name: Test Specimens for High Strength Steel
text: All high strength steel parts heat treated at or above 1241 MPa ultimate tensile strength shall include appropriate test specimens from the same heat of material as the part.

name: Test Specimen Tracking
text: These test specimens shall accompany the parts through the entire fabrication cycle to ensure that the desired properties are obtained.

name: Hydrogen Embrittlement Bake-Out
text: When acid cleaning baths or plating processes are used on high strength steel parts, the parts shall be baked at 190 deg C for not less than 23 hours to alleviate hydrogen embrittlement.

name: Restriction on Low Fracture Toughness Materials
text: Materials with low fracture toughness in the predicted operating environment, such as some plastics, shall not be used.

name: Restriction on Shock-Sensitive Materials
text: Materials susceptible to cracking due to shock loads or shock loads combined with low temperatures shall not be used near pyrotechnically actuated devices.

name: Minimize Use of Magnetic Materials
text: To minimize possible interactions with experiments or with the earth's magnetic field, magnetic materials shall be used only where necessary for equipment operation.

name: Restrictions on High-Altitude Insulating Materials
text: For vehicles that will operate at altitudes above 1000 kilometers, insulating materials or finishes having a resistivity greater than 10 megohm-meters shall not be used except in applications where charge buildup will not be excessive.

name: Minimum Wall Thickness for Sheet Metal and Composites
text: Except for honeycomb panels, wall thickness of sheet metal and wall thickness on composite parts shall, where practicable, be greater than 0.5 millimeters to minimize the possibility of handling damage.

name: Honeycomb Venting Requirements
text: Honeycomb shall be vented to prevent excessive blow-off forces in vacuum.

name: Surface Treatments for Corrosion Resistance
text: Any surface treatments or coatings used shall be such that completed components shall be resistant to corrosion. The design goal should be that there would be no harmful corrosion of the completed components or assemblies when exposed to moderately humid or mildly corrosive environments while unprotected during manufacture or handling.

name: Definition of Harmful Corrosion
text: Harmful corrosion shall be construed as being any type of corrosion which interferes with meeting the specified performance of the equipment or its associated parts.

name: Protective Methods and Materials
text: Protective methods and materials for cleaning, surface treatment, and applications of protective coatings shall be in accordance with MIL-F-7179.

name: Prohibition on Cadmium and Zinc Coatings
text: Cadmium and zinc coatings shall not be used.

name: Chromium Plating Requirements
text: Chromium plating shall be in accordance with QQ-C-320.

name: Nickel Plating Requirements
text: Nickel plating shall be in accordance with QQ-N-290 or MIL-C-26074.

name: Anodic Treatment of Aluminum
text: Anodic treatment of aluminum and aluminum alloys shall be in accordance with MIL-A-8625.

name: Anodic Treatment of Magnesium
text: Anodic treatment of magnesium shall be in accordance with MIL-M-45202.

name: Corrosion Protection of Magnesium
text: Corrosion protection of magnesium shall be in accordance with MIL-M-3171.

name: Chemical Films for Aluminum
text: Chemical films for aluminum and aluminum alloys shall be in accordance with MIL-C-5541.

name: Deployables Self-Supporting
text: Deployables shall, where practicable, be designed so that they are self supporting when placed in any orientation relative to gravity, while in either the stowed or deployed configuration.

name: Ground Test Motive Force
text: Deployables shall be designed with sufficient motive force to permit full operation during ground testing without depending upon the assistance of gravity.

name: Deployable Redundancy
text: Deployables shall utilize redundancy, where practicable, in the design to improve the reliability of deployment.

name: Redundant Springs Consideration
text: Techniques such as redundant springs or the use of a backup deployment device shall be considered to satisfy the redundancy requirement.

name: CG Alignment for Rotating Deployables
text: Where a device rotates after deployment, the design shall, where practicable, be such that the center of gravity is coincident with the axis of rotation.

name: Controlled or Restrained Deployment
text: For all deployables, the deployment motion shall, where practicable, be controlled or restrained for the full range of travel.

name: Kick-Off Springs
text: Kick-off springs or other suitable devices shall, where practicable, be used to initiate deployment motion.

name: Kick-Off Spring Stroke
text: Kick-off springs shall have a stroke long enough to ensure complete disengagement of the deployable from its retention mechanism.

name: Field Joints for Disassembly
text: Field joints shall be provided, where practicable, to permit disassembly of deployables and rotating or translating elements.

name: Sequential Pyro Events
text: Deployables requiring discrete sequential motions initiated by separate pyrotechnic events shall have each event separately ground commanded or have a backup ground command.

name: Cable Guidance
text: Where cables are used in the deployment mechanism, they shall be adequately guided and supported by fairleads.

name: Pulley Guards
text: All pulleys shall utilize pulley guards which extend to the tangency points of the cable.

name: No Dependency Between Deployables
text: Where two or more deployables are used on a vehicle, the deployment of one shall not be dependent upon the successful deployment of the other, unless unavoidable.

name: Redundant Release for Mission-Critical Sequential Deployables
text: Where sequential dependency cannot be avoided and the obstructed deployable is mission critical, a fully redundant release device and backup deployment mechanism shall be provided.

name: Positive Retention in Stowed and Deployed Positions
text: Positive retention provisions shall be provided for deployables in the stowed and deployed positions.

name: Consider Deflections in Attachment Design
text: The effects of deflections such as centrifugal forces or differential thermal growth shall be considered in the design of deployable attachments.

name: Avoid Binding-Prone Devices
text: Devices subject to binding due to misalignment, adverse tolerances, or contamination shall not be used.

name: Avoid Slip Joints
text: Slip joints shall be avoided, where practicable.

name: Use Self-Aligning Features
text: Self-aligning features such as self-aligning bearings and rod ends shall be used, where practicable, to preclude binding.

name: No Continuous Hinges for Large Panels
text: Continuous hinges such as piano hinges shall not be used for large deployable panels.

name: Avoid Ejection-Type Release Mechanisms
text: Release mechanisms which permit ejection of parts away from the vehicle shall be avoided, where practicable.

name: Minimize Latch Resistance Peaking
text: The design of latching devices shall be such that peaking of resistance near the end of travel is minimized.

name: Avoid Leaf Spring Latches
text: Leaf spring latches which become the primary element for reacting deployment or rebound loads shall be avoided, where practicable.

name: Avoid Permanent Magnet Catches
text: Catches using a permanent magnet as the holding element shall be avoided, where practicable.

name: Retention Device Fatigue Stress Limits
text: The design and materials used for the retention devices shall be such that the stresses are maintained sufficiently below the fatigue endurance limit to avoid fatigue failures due to cyclic design load levels and environmental exposure.

name: Prevention of Cold Welding and Friction Welding
text: Retention and release devices shall be designed to preclude cold welding and friction welding.

name: Minimization of Contact Pressures
text: For surfaces that slide or separate during operational use, the contact pressures at the interfaces shall be minimized consistent with providing adequate ascent stiffness.

name: Prevention of Galling or Seizure
text: These surfaces shall be fabricated from appropriate materials and lubricated so as to prevent galling or seizure.

name: Minimum Contact Area for Pressure Calculations
text: Where contact areas may be reduced from the nominal as a result of tolerance build-up, the minimum area which could occur shall be used in determining contact pressure.

name: Pin Pullers in Double Shear
text: Where pin pullers are used, they shall be designed to be in double shear.

name: Pin Puller Misalignment Loads
text: The design, installation, and checkout procedures for pin pullers shall ensure that loads due to misalignment are within design limits.

name: Pin Puller Retraction Margin
text: A minimum retraction force margin of safety of 100 percent shall be maintained for all nonexplosive pin pullers.

name: Functional Margins for Cartridge Actuated Pin Pullers
text: Functional margins of cartridge actuated pin pullers shall comply with DOD-E-83578.

name: Release Device Stroke Requirements
text: Release devices, such as pin pullers, shall have sufficient stroke so that complete release is attained under worst case tolerances and environmental conditions.

name: Pin Puller Stroke Requirement
text: Pin pullers shall retract at least 2 millimeters beyond the point of release under worst case tolerances and environmental conditions.

name: Redundant Release Devices
text: Redundant release devices shall be used, where practicable.
guidance: (An example is a toggle release mechanism where activation of either pin puller permits release.)

name: Pyrotechnic Devices per DOD-EL83578
text: Cartridge actuated device designs and their application shall comply with DOD-EL83578.

name: Redundant Pyrotechnic Release Devices
text: Redundant pyrotechnic (release) devices shall be used, where practicable.

name: Test Fixture Compatibility
text: Fixtures used to assist in fabrication and testing shall be designed in conjunction with the deployable device to ensure compatibility.

name: Minimize Influence of Supplemental Supports
text: Supplemental supports shall be designed so that their influence on the operation of the mechanism is minimized.

name: Test Fixture Measurement Provisions
text: Test fixtures shall incorporate provisions to measure torque vs angle and time vs angle, or equivalent linear measurements.

name: Test Fixture Safety Interlocks
text: Where practicable, test fixtures shall have interlocks or other safety features incorporated to preclude damage to the moving mechanical assembly or deployable in the event of testing malfunctions.

name: Tethers and Backup Supports
text: Tethers and supports shall be incorporated as backup features to preclude damage in the event of failure.

name: Use Self-Aligning Bearings
text: For deployables, hinges, and linkages, self-aligning bearings shall be used, where practicable, to preclude binding due to misalignments.

name: Bearings Not for Electrical Current
text: Bearings shall not be used for ground current return paths or to carry electrical current.

name: Use Corrosion-Resistant Steel for Ferrous Bearings
text: All ferrous material bearings shall employ, where practicable, a corrosion-resistant steel that is in accordance with QQ-S-763.

name: Rolling Element Bearing Material
text: Rolling element bearings shall, where practicable, be of 440C stainless steel; however, 52100 or M50 steels may be employed providing they are suitably protected from corrosion.

name: Rolling Element Bearing Hardness
text: Rolling element bearings shall have a minimum hardness of Rockwell C58.

name: CEVM Material for Critical Bearings
text: Ball bearings used in applications where low torque ripple is required or where fatigue life is critical shall, where practicable, be fabricated of consumable electrode vacuum melted (CEVM) material.

name: ABEC 7 Bearings for Critical Applications
text: Bearings used in critical applications such as reaction wheels, control moment gyros, gimbals, de-spin mechanisms, and pointing devices shall meet ABEC 7, 7P or 7T tolerance or better.

name: Nonstandard Bearings Equivalent to ABEC 7
text: Nonstandard bearings or thin sectioned bearings where AFBMA tolerances do not apply shall have the manufacturer's precision level most nearly equivalent to ABEC 7.

name: ABEC 5 for Noncritical Deployables
text: Bearings used in noncritical applications such as one time use deployables shall, where practicable, meet ABEC 5 or better.

name: Stainless Bearings per MIL-B-81793
text: Stainless steel bearings shall, where practicable, also be in accordance with MIL-B-81793.

name: Bearing Design Considerations
text: Ball bearing selection, mounting, and preloading shall be based on the following design considerations:
a. maximum combined axial, radial, and moment loads sustained during all operational modes.
b. Stiffness requirements
c.Effects of temperature, temperature gradients, fits, tolerances, and initial preload on torque, stiffness, and life
d. Lubrication
e. Wear
f. Smoothness of operation (torque ripple)
g. Friction torques, considering breakaway and running, in the installed state
h. Reliability and life

name: Bearing Design Substantiation
text: The design of each ball bearing installation shall be substantiated by analysis and either development tests or previous usage.

name: Consideration of Bearing Design Factors
text: The materials, stresses, stiffness, fatigue life, preload, and possible binding under normal, as well as the most severe combined loading conditions, and other expected environmental conditions shall be considered.

name: Preload Variation Factors
text: Alignments, fits, tolerances, thermal and load induced distortions, and other conditions shall be considered in determining preload variations.

name: Analysis of Fits and Temperature Effects
text: An analysis of the effects of fits and temperatures shall be performed where the preload value is critical to meet either life, friction, or stiffness requirements.

name: Bearing Fatigue Life Survival Probability
text: Bearing fatigue life calculations shall be based on a survival probability of 99.95 percent when subjected to maximum time varying loads.

name: Bearing Material and Lubrication Correction Factors
text: Appropriate correction factors shall be included to account for the selected bearing materials and lubrication parameters.

name: Bearing Retainer Friction Contribution
text: Bearing retainer design shall provide an acceptable contribution to bearing friction torque and torque variation.

name: Hertzian Stress Limits for Noncritical Applications
text: For noncritical applications, such as most deployables, if nonquiet running is acceptable, the mean Hertzian contact stress shall not exceed 2758 megapascals (400,000 psi) when subjected to the yield load.

name: Operational Hertzian Stress Limits
text: During operation, the mean Hertzian stress shall not exceed 2310 megapascals (335,000 psi).

name: Bearing Ultimate Load Requirements
text: The bearings shall be designed to withstand the ultimate load without fracture.

name: Yield and Ultimate Factors of Safety
text: The yield and ultimate factors of safety shall be as specified in 3.4.1.5.

name: Stress Limits for Quiet or Low Torque Ripple Applications
text: For these applications, in addition to the requirements of Paragraph 3.2.3.1.1 bearing races and balls shall be designed so that stress levels are below the levels that would cause unacceptable permanent deformation during application of ascent loads.

name: Hertzian Stress Limits for Bearings Carrying Ascent Loads
text: Where ball bearing deformation is required to carry a portion or all of the ascent loads, and where smoothness of operation is required on orbit, the mean Hertzian stress levels of the bearing steel shall not exceed 2310 megapascals (335,000 psi) when subjected to the yield load.

name: Containment of Contact Ellipses
text: The upper and lower extremes of the contact ellipses shall be contained by the raceways.

name: Race Stress and Shoulder Height Analysis
text: The stress and shoulder height requirements of the races shall be analyzed for both nominal and off-nominal bearing tolerances.

name: Serialization and Measurement Recording
text: For subsequent analysis and for quality control, these bearings shall be serialized and measurements critical to their operation shall be recorded.

name: Recording of Critical Bearing Parameters
text: Depending on the application and its requirements, consideration shall be given to recording preload, low speed torque, inside diameter, outside diameter, angle, radial play or control curvatures, raceway roundness, ball size and roundness, raceway surface finishes, and hardness.

name: Reuse of Bearings for Multiple Flights
text: The design of bearings that are to be used for a number of flights shall be substantiated by analysis and either development tests or previous usage.

name: Run-Out Tolerances for Bearing Alignment
text: Run-out tolerances on shaft and housing diameters and shoulders shall be established in accordance with the needs of the application and the sensitivity of the bearing to misalignment.

name: Misalignment Limits for Sensitive Bearings
text: Overall misalignment of inner plus outer rings of these bearings shall, where practicable, not exceed 0.3 milliradians.

name: Misalignment Limits for Other Bearings
text: Other bearings shall, where practicable, have overall misalignment not exceeding 1 milliradian.

name: Selection Criteria for Other Bearing Types
text: Selection of other bearing types such as roller, needle, or journal, shall be based on maximum combined loads, temperature excursions, effects of temperature on fits and tolerances, stiffness, lubrication, smoothness of operation, friction torques, and reliability over the design life.

name: Substantiation of Bearing Installations
text: The design of each bearing installation shall be substantiated by analysis and either development tests or previous usage.

name: Bearing Design Considerations
text: The materials, stresses, stiffness, fatigue life, preload, and possible binding under normal, as well as most severe combined loading conditions, and other expected environmental conditions shall be considered.

name: Lubrication Required for All Contacting Surfaces
text: Lubrication shall be provided by greases, liquids, solid film lubricants, or combinations thereof for all contacting surfaces having relative motion.

name: Lubricant Selection Criteria
text: The selection of lubricants for moving mechanical assemblies shall be based on
a. coefficient of friction
b. vacuum behavior
c. depletion
d. temperature limits, viscosity
h. outgassing
i. corrosion protection
j. polymerization
l. cleanliness
m. run-in requirements, and
p. Compatibility of the lubricant with other materials , particularly other lubricants if used

name: Lubricant Shall Not Cause Detrimental Effects
text: The lubricant chosen shall not cause detrimental effects on the moving mechanical assembly during or after operation at ambient conditions.

name: Vent Paths for Liquid Lubricants
text: The vent paths from all liquid lubricants shall be designed such that the outgassing products do not impinge directly on critical surfaces.

name: Lubricant Selection Based on Development Tests
text: The selection of the lubricant for use in the critical moving mechanical assembly shall be based upon development tests demonstrating adequate lubrication under all specified operating conditions over the design lifetime.

name: Lubricant and Process Documentation
text: The lubricant selected, and the processes used in cleaning parts and applying the lubricant shall be delineated.

name: Corrosion Inhibitors for M50 and 52100
text: Lubricants used with M50 or 52100 gear materials shall include corrosion inhibitors which prevent corrosion when the assembly is humidity tested in accordance with MIL-STD-1540.

name: Maximize Lubricant Film Thickness
text: In moving mechanical assemblies utilizing grease or liquid lubrication in rolling element bearings, the lubricant film thickness shall be maximized consistent with the following: a. the lubricant selected, b. the range of operating conditions including load, torque, speed, and temperature, and c. bearing parameters such as size, number of balls, and ball size as they relate to weight and volume constraints.

name: Avoid Boundary Lubrication
text: Bearings operating in the boundary lubrication regime, i.e., contact of asperities, shall be avoided, where practicable.

name: Boundary Lubrication Requirements
text: If bearings must be operated in the boundary lubrication regime, a boundary lubricant with good anti-wear characteristics shall be used.

name: Reservoir Attachment for Lubricant Flow
text: Where bearing lubricant reservoirs are used, the reservoir shall be attached, where practicable, to an area of relatively high temperature to enhance molecular and surface flow into the bearing.

name: Substantiation of Lubricant Transfer Mechanism
text: The design adequacy of the lubricant transfer mechanism shall be substantiated by analysis and either development tests or previous usage.

name: Lubricant Transfer Mechanism Analysis Factors
text: This analysis shall take into account the test results and, as applicable, the effects of zero g, position and surface area of the reservoir, temperature gradients, venting, reservoir material, amount of lubricant stored in the reservoir, surface migration, pressure, free molecular flow, material surface roughness, porosity, and capillary action.

name: Verification of Lubricant Transport Mechanisms
text: Bearing lubrication tests and supporting analyses shall be used to show that the chosen lubricant transport mechanisms such as surface migration, vaporization, and wick action provide effective lubricant films over the expected operating temperatures, thermal gradients, and internal environments.

name: Verification of EHD Lubrication Regime
text: If providing adequate life of bearings depends on their operating in an elasto-hydrodynamic (EHD) lubrication regime and not in the boundary lubrication regime, and it cannot be clearly shown by analysis that the bearing operating range is well within the regime, then a test method, such as contact resistance measurements, shall be used to establish that an EHD film is being generated.

name: Control of Lubricant Migration Through Seals
text: When liquid lubrication is used, the design shall ensure that migration of the lubricant through the seals is not excessive or detrimental to the vehicle.

name: Dry Film Lubricant Application Process
text: Application of dry film lubricants shall be by an appropriate process that provides a predictable, uniform, and repeatable lubricant film.

name: Corrosion Resistant Materials for Dry Film Bearings
text: Corrosion resistant materials shall be used in bearings employing dry film lubricants.

name: Protect MoS2 from Humidity
text: Consideration shall be given to protection of molybdenum disulfide dry film lubricants from adverse effects due to exposure to atmospheric humidity.

name: Avoid Testing in Humid Environment
text: Testing in a humid environment shall, where practicable, either be avoided or minimized.

name: Hard Coating Application Process
text: Hard coatings shall be applied by an appropriate process such as ion implantation or chemical vapor deposition that assures the coating will not flake off under maximum stress.

name: Hydraulic Fluid Conformance
text: Fluids used in hydraulic systems shall be in conformance with MIL-H-6083 or MIL-H-5605.

name: Brush and Slip Ring Interface Performance
text: Electrical brushes and slip ring assemblies shall utilize interface geometry and materials that have demonstrated satisfactory performance in ground testing or space applications with similar requirements.

name: Prohibition on All-Carbon Brushes
text: Brushes that are nominally all carbon shall not be used.

name: Brush Lubrication Requirements
text: Electrical brushes shall be lubricated either by dry film lubricant that is a composite with the brush material or by a liquid lubricant that is impregnated into the brush material or retained in the area of the brush.

name: Brush and Slip Ring Design Considerations
text: Electrical brush and slip ring design shall be based on, but not limited to, considerations including interface geometry, contact forces, wear rate, contact force control, zero g effects, materials, surface speeds, outgassing, sealing provisions, wear debris control, debris barriers, electrical current density, voltage level, contact resistance, electrical noise, temperature, contact area, lubrication, corrosion prevention, and ability to conduct accelerated testing.

name: Design Verification Testing for Brushes and Slip Rings
text: Design verification testing of brushes and commutator or slip ring assemblies shall be conducted to demonstrate that the lubricant is not significantly deteriorated or driven from the areas requiring lubrication by adverse thermal, gravity forces, or other conditions; and that wear rates, wear debris, electrical noise level, friction torque, and lubricant loss are compatible with design requirements.

name: Electronic Equipment Standards Compliance
text: Electronic equipment shall be in accordance with DOD-E-8983.

name: External Wiring Standards Compliance
text: Wiring external to equipment enclosures shall be in accordance with DOD-W-83575.

name: Wiring Harness Interface Dimensions
text: Where wiring harnesses cross a moving or rotating interface, the installation drawings shall define dimensions including loop sizes and distances to attachments, if applicable.

name: Harness Attachment Clamp Requirements
text: Attachment clamps shall be provided sufficiently close to any loops so that movement of the harness into the path of motion of the moving mechanical assembly cannot occur under any conditions.

name: Prohibition on Strain-Energy Elements
text: Wire bundles crossing a moving or rotating interface shall not contain strain-energy elements specifically added to assist deployment.

name: Grounding of Moving Mechanical Assemblies
text: All metal parts of the moving mechanical assembly shall be appropriately grounded to vehicle structure so that charge build-up in space and shock hazards on the ground can be minimized.

name: Determination of Total Current Draw
text: The total current drawn from the power source during each mode of operation shall be determined to preclude inadvertent electrical overloads.

name: Current Draw Measurements Across Voltage Range
text: These determinations or measurements shall be made at the minimum, nominal, and maximum voltage of the power source, and under the most severe environmental conditions.

name: Overload Protection Requirements
text: Overload protection, when required, shall be a part of the vehicle electrical power control subsystem.

name: Ground Command Reset Capability
text: A capability shall be provided to reset power disconnects by ground command.

name: AC Motor Compliance
text: Alternating current motors shall conform to MIL-M-13787.

name: DC Motor Compliance and Brushless Preference
text: Direct current motors shall conform to MIL-M-8609 or MIL-M-13786.

name: Brush Motor Application Considerations
text: Applications for conventional brush commutated motors shall consider lubrication, wear, input voltage range, and electromagnetic interference compatibility.

name: Motor Characterization for Critical Applications
text: For applications where the motor performance is critical to the mission success, the design shall be based on a complete motor characterization.

name: Motor Characterization Parameters
text: The motor characterization shall include rotor inertia, friction and damping parameters, back-EMF constant or torque constant, time constant, torque characteristics, speed versus torque curves, thermal dissipation, temperature effects, and, where applicable, analysis to demonstrate adequate margin against back driving.

name: Motor-Level Characterization Prior to Integration
text: For applications where the motor is integrated into a higher assembly, the motor characterization shall be performed at the motor level prior to the integration.

name: Motor Mount Heat Transfer Accommodation
text: Where motors are operated at high duty cycles, the design of the motor mount shall accommodate the heat transfer from the motor case to surrounding structure.

name: Stepper Motor Detent Torque and Holding Capability
text: In cases where the magnetic holding capability of the motor is used to hold the load in position, the design shall be based on the detent torque at each discrete rotor position for both the clockwise and counterclockwise direction.

name: Avoid Pulsing at Load Natural Frequency
text: Where stepper motors are used to drive a load, pulsing the stepper motor at a repetition rate that is at or near the natural frequency of the load shall be avoided.

name: Helical Spring Compliance
text: Helical springs shall be in accordance with MIL-S-13572 and MIL-STD-29.

name: Compression Spring Captivation
text: Helical compression springs shall, where practicable, be enclosed or otherwise captivated to prevent buckling, and to provide motive power even if broken.

name: Leaf Spring Attachment Stress Reduction
text: The attachments for retaining leaf springs shall be designed to reduce stress concentrations by such features as rounding of sharp corners or keeping mounting holes away from highly stressed areas.

name: Spring Fatigue and Temperature Effects
text: Spring design shall consider fatigue life and the effects of temperature on spring performance.

name: Spring Creep Avoidance
text: To reduce the possibility of a reduction of potential energy due to creep, springs which are stored in a stressed condition shall be designed to maintain stress levels below the material proportional limit.

name: Redundant Spring Usage
text: Redundant springs, capable of working independently, shall be used in all applications, where practicable.

name: Dry Film Lubrication for Low Friction
text: When minimum friction is desirable, springs shall be dry film lubricated.

name: Dry Film Lubricant Material Restrictions
text: The dry film lubricant shall be selected to avoid corrosion, and shall not contain carbon or powdered metal.

name: Deformable Damper Inspection and Replacement
text: Deformable material damper design shall permit inspection and replacement of the deformable material following ground tests.

name: Deformable Material Tolerance Effects
text: Deformable material damper design shall consider the effect of the deformable material tolerances on the final position of the mechanism with respect to its desired position.

name: Viscous Damper Fluid Cleanliness
text: Viscous damper fluids shall be maintained to at least a cleanliness of Level 200 as defined in MIL-STD-1246.

name: Vacuum Filling of Viscous Dampers
text: All viscous dampers shall be vacuum filled to preclude entrapment of air.

name: Filter Use in Viscous Dampers
text: Filters shall be used in viscous dampers unless they are incompatible with the viscosity of the fluid being used or the design of the damper.

name: Force/Torque Margin Calculation for Viscous Dampers
text: The calculation of the force or torque margin in assemblies with viscous dampers shall include, but not be limited to, the seal friction due to mechanical compression of elastomers, fluid pressure on the elastomers, and possible changes in static and dynamic friction due to storage time.

name: Viscous Damper Temperature Effects
text: Viscous damper design shall make appropriate provisions for changes in fluid volume and viscosity with temperature.

name: Viscous Damper Leakage Prevention
text: As a minimum, dampers shall either incorporate redundant seals or be hermetically enclosed to prevent leakage during the entire on-orbit life of the vehicle.

name: Eddy Current Damper Temperature-Range Damping Requirement
text: Eddy current dampers shall be designed to provide the required damping over the design temperature range.

name: AGMA Compliance and Lubrication Requirements for Gears
text: All gears used in moving mechanical assemblies shall be in accordance with the standards of the American Gear Manufacturers Association (AGMA). The lubrication requirements of Paragraph 3.2.4 are applicable to gears.

name: Use of Hunting Tooth Gear Ratios
text: Hunting tooth gear ratios shall be used, where the application is appropriate, to distribute wear.

name: Gear Tooth Count Selection for Wear Distribution
text: The number of teeth on each gear shall be selected, within the limits of the gear ratio requirement, to maximize the number of revolutions before meshing of the same two teeth.

name: Gear Design and Selection Considerations
text: Gearing design and selection shall be based on the following design considerations: (a) Tooth pitting, Brinelling, and bending stresses under nominal and peak operating loads; (b) Impact tooth loads from maximum combined axial, radial, and moment loads sustained during ground handling, launch, on orbit, or other modes; (c) Backlash; (d) Precision including position errors and transmission errors (smoothness of motion); (e) Stiffness; (f) Inertia; (g) Lubrication; (h) Effects of temperature and temperature gradients on quality of lubrication and gear contact pattern; (i) Effects of tooth geometry on specific sliding and wear; (j) Friction and friction variation (torque ripple); (k) Undercutting and tooth profile modifications; (l) Gear mounting, misalignment, face load distribution, and variation in operating center distance; (m) Materials, manufacturing and heat treatment processes, and finish coatings; (n) Service life, duty cycle, failure modes, and reliability.

name: Harmonic Drive Anti-Ratcheting Requirement
text: The harmonic drive shall be designed so it is not subjected to loads that cause ratcheting.

name: Harmonic Drive Element Compliance
text: Harmonic drive elements shall meet the applicable requirements stated herein. For example, the wave generator bearing shall meet the requirements of Paragraph 3.2.3.

name: Harmonic Drive Lubrication for Long Life
text: For long life applications, sufficient lubricant shall be provided to the bearings and to the gear teeth to ensure proper operation throughout the life cycle.

name: Precision Gear Anti-Backlash and Quality Level
text: For precision gears, such as in fine pointing mechanisms, anti-backlash gearing shall, where practicable, be used.

name: Matched Gear Set Identification
text: Where gears are required to be matched sets, they shall be identified and marked as such.

name: Fastening Systems Standard Compliance
text: Fastening systems shall be in accordance with MIL-STD-1515.

name: Threaded Parts Standard Compliance
text: Threaded parts shall be in accordance with MIL-S-7742 or MIL-S-8879.

name: Thread Engagement Requirements
text: A minimum engagement of five full threads is required for threaded attachments; or for through bolts, the threaded ends shall protrude a minimum of two full threads beyond the end of the nut.

name: Minimum Screw Size and Blind Hole Considerations
text: Screw sizes smaller than 3.6 millimeters (No. 8) in diameter shall be avoided, where practicable. Where there are areas which may be sensitive to debris generated during assembly of threaded parts, blind holes should be considered.

name: Thread Tolerance Control for Blind Holes
text: Tolerances shall be controlled to prevent threaded parts from bottoming in blind holes.

name: Use of Positive Locking Devices
text: Positive locking devices shall be used on all fasteners. Preferred positive locking devices are bent tab washers, cotter pins, safety wire, self-locking threads, or self-locking provisions by means of plastic material contained in the nut, bolt, or screw. Self-locking nuts are preferred to bolts or screws that contain plastic material for use as a locking device.

name: Prohibition on Locking Compounds for Locking
text: Where other locking devices are practicable, locking compounds shall not be used on fasteners to provide locking.

name: Prohibition on Locking Compounds Near Moving Surfaces
text: Locking compounds shall not be used in areas where excess compound could migrate to surfaces which must remain free to move.

name: Avoidance of Interference-Fit Self-Locking Devices
text: Self-locking devices which depend upon an interference fit between metallic threads shall be avoided, where practicable, in applications where particulate contamination may cause damage or degradation to the equipment or vehicle.

name: Preload Measurement Techniques for Critical Fasteners
text: Where preload in fasteners is critical, strain gauges, crush washers, or equivalent techniques shall be used, where practicable, in lieu of torque wrench setting of the preload.

name: Safety Wiring and Cotter Pin Standard Compliance
text: Safety wiring and cotter pins shall be in accordance with MS-33540.

name: Safety Wiring Depiction and Preference for Through Bolts
text: Drawings shall clearly depict the safety wiring method and configuration used. Through bolts or screws with locknuts are preferred to threaded inserts.

name: Use of Threaded Inserts in Soft or Damage-Prone Materials
text: Threaded inserts shall be used in applications that require tapped holes in aluminum, magnesium, plastic, or other materials that are susceptible to galling or thread damage.

name: Minimum Engagement for Self-Locking Features
text: When self-locking features are used, the screw length shall be sufficient to fully engage the locking device with a minimum of two turns under worst case tolerances.

name: Run-In Torque and Reuse Limits for Self-Locking Features
text: When self-locking features are used, an allowable range of run-in torque, or the maximum number of reuses that would still ensure an adequate lock, shall be specified.

name: Prohibition on Spring or Star Type Lock Washers
text: Spring type or star type lock washers shall not be used.

name: Prohibition on Friction-Based Locking for Adjustable Fittings
text: Adjustable fittings or mounting plates which use oversized holes or slotted holes to provide adjustment shall not be dependent upon friction between the fitting or mounting plate and the mounting surface to provide locking.

name: Prohibition on Diamond Type Serrations
text: Diamond type serrations shall not be used.

name: Retention Requirements for Rotating Bolt Shafts
text: When the shaft of a bolt is used as a rotating element in a rotating joint, a castle nut with cotter pin, or a locknut with deformed threads shall be used for retention of the bolt.

name: End Play Requirement for Rotating Bolts
text: The grip length of the rotating bolt shall ensure that sufficient end play is provided to preclude binding.

name: Fixed Pivot Bolt Requirements
text: When the shaft of a bolt is used as a fixed pivotal element in a rotating joint, the bolt shall either be a shoulder bolt or the bolt shall pass through a spacer.

name: End Play Requirement for Shoulder Bolts and Spacers
text: The grip length of the shoulder bolt or the length of the spacer shall ensure that sufficient end play is provided to preclude binding when the self-locking nut is tightened.

name: Prohibition on Split or Rolled Spring-Action Pins as Pivots
text: Split or rolled spring-action pins shall not be used as pivots for rotating joints.

name: Retention Requirements for Spring-Action Pins
text: Where split or rolled spring-action pins are used in other applications, a positive means of retaining the pin, such as staking the edges of the hole, shall be utilized.

name: Prohibition on Locking Compounds for Pivot Pins
text: Locking compounds shall not be used as the retention method for pivot pins.

name: Avoidance of Snap Rings Where Positive Retention Exists
text: Snap rings shall be avoided where a more positive means of retention can be used.

name: Prohibition on Snap Rings for Pin Retention Under Moment Loads
text: Snap rings shall not be used to retain pins in linkages or other applications where there is a possibility that moment loads may be imposed on the snap ring.

name: Snap Ring Groove Cleanliness with Dry Film Lubrication
text: Where snap rings are used in the presence of dry film lubrication, care shall be taken to ensure that no dry film lubricant is deposited in the groove for the snap ring.

name: Replacement of Snap Rings Upon Reassembly
text: New snap rings shall be used each time the assembly, or portion thereof which includes the snap ring, is disassembled and reassembled.

name: Structural Yield Factor of Safety for Mechanical Stops
text: Mechanical stops or shoulders and associated attachments shall be designed to a structural yield factor of safety, based on static analysis, of at least 2.0 for maximum impact loads that occur upon full extension, actuation, or stopping of moving mechanical assemblies.

name: Impact Load Modeling and Dynamic Analysis Requirements
text: Impact loads shall account for uncertainties in model parameters, analysis methodology, and any other effects such as amplified inertia loads that may be transmitted through gear trains. If it can be shown that the dynamic analysis inherently accounts for dynamic load amplification as a result of the impact, ordinary factors of safety as specified elsewhere in this document may be used.

name: Protection of Gear Teeth and Drive Mechanisms from Stop Transients
text: The design shall ensure that the stop transients do not over-stress gear teeth or drive mechanisms.

name: Adjustment Requirements for Linkages and Stops
text: Adjustments shall be provided in linkages and stops to ensure that the travel of the moving mechanical assembly is not restricted before contact with the stop by tolerance buildups, thermal distortions, and other uncertainties.

name: Structural Design Analysis Requirements
text: Structural design of each moving mechanical assembly shall be based upon a load analysis, stress analysis, fatigue analysis, and the substantiating test program.

name: Fracture Mechanics Analysis Requirement
text: Fracture mechanics analysis shall be performed if the brittle failure mode cannot be avoided in the design.

name: Stress Analysis Considerations
text: The stress analysis shall include considerations of structural stiffness, elastic or plastic deformations, and thermal distortions.

name: Structural Strength and Rigidity Requirements
text: The design shall possess sufficient strength, rigidity, and other necessary characteristics required to survive all loads and environmental conditions that exist within the envelope of mission requirements, and to meet any alignment constraints or pointing accuracy requirements that may be imposed for successful performance of the system.

name: Survivability of Loads and Environments
text: The assembly shall survive these loads and environments in a manner that does not reduce the probability of the successful completion of the mission.

name: Yield Load Strength Requirements
text: The structure shall be designed to have sufficient strength to withstand simultaneously the yield loads, applied temperature, and other environmental conditions, without experiencing gross yielding or detrimental deformation.

name: Ultimate Load Strength Requirements
text: The structure shall be designed to withstand simultaneously the ultimate loads, applied temperature, and other environmental conditions without collapse. Refer to Paragraph 3.4.1.5 for acceleration levels, yield and ultimate factors of safety, and margins of safety, and to Paragraph 3.6.3 for fitting factors.

name: Material Property Source Requirements
text: Material strength and other mechanical and physical properties shall be selected from MIL-HDBK-5 and MIL-HDBK-17 or from contractor test values, where appropriate.

name: Contractor Test Value Statistical Basis
text: When contractor test values are used, they shall be based on a sufficient number of tests to establish the mechanical properties on a statistical basis.

name: Allowable Material Strength Effects
text: Allowable material strengths used in the design shall reflect the effects of load, temperature, and time associated with the design environment.

name: Material Strength Allowable Values
text: The following material strength allowable values shall be used: (a) For single load path primary structures, the A values in MIL-HDBK-5 shall be used. (b) For multiple load path and secondary structures, the B values in MIL-HDBK-5 may be used.

name: Worst Case Operational Load Derivation
text: The loads shall be derived by considering all worst case operational conditions such as lift-off, ascent, ignition, shutdown, deployment, reentry, and vibration conditions which may be induced by the launch vehicle or injection stage.

name: Orbital Load Derivation Requirements
text: In addition, orbital loads which may be induced by thermal conditions, spin up, separation, impulsive forces, propulsive variations, nutation, wobble motions, or other control system associated conditions shall be included.

name: Composite Material Property Source Requirements
text: Composite material strengths, and other mechanical or physical properties, shall be selected from reliable sources, such as MIL-HDBK-17 or data determined in approved contractor development test programs.

name: Composite Anisotropy Consideration
text: The anisotropy of typical laminated composite structural elements shall be accounted for when establishing laminate material properties and failure modes.

name: Laminate Strength Appropriateness
text: The laminate strength and other mechanical properties used shall be appropriate for the critical structural modes of failure and environmental conditions.

name: Composite Material Property Testing Requirement
text: For cases where applicable material properties do not exist, testing is required to establish such values.

name: Composite Coupon Variability and Scaling
text: The variability of small coupon specimen properties and the scaling to full-size composite structure shall be addressed to establish realistic design properties.

name: Composite Critical Region Failure Considerations
text: In particular, the potential effects of low interlaminar strength, the lack of ductility, local yielding, and sensitivity to impact and handling damage shall be addressed in the critical regions of the structure.

name: Composite Primary Structure Proof Testing
text: Composite primary structures shall be acceptance proof tested at minimum loads of 1.1 times the design limit loads.

name: Adhesive and Polymer Property Source Requirements
text: Mechanical and physical properties of adhesives and polymers shall be selected from authorized sources of reference such as MIL-HDBK-23 or data determined in approved contractor development test programs.

name: Nonmetallic Material Selection Standards
text: Nonmetallic structural material shall be selected from JSC-07572 or verified for acceptability by methods of SPEC-SP-R-0022.

name: Allowables Basis for Nonmetallic Structures
text: The design allowables basis for primary and secondary nonmetallic structure shall correspond with 'A' and 'B' levels, respectively, as defined in MIL-HDBK-5, wherever possible.

name: Pressurized Component Standard Compliance
text: Pressurized components shall be in accordance with MIL-STD-1522.

name: Diagnostic Instrumentation for Failure Mode Determination
text: Sufficient diagnostic instrumentation shall be developed and provided, where practicable, as part of the moving mechanical assembly to determine the mode of failure should an on-orbit failure occur. These may be such devices as strain gauges, temperature sensors, pressure transducers, position indicators, potentiometers, switches, tachometers, accelerometers, or current monitors.

name: Motor Current Instrumentation Requirement
text: When an electrical motor, other than a stepper motor, is used, the motor current shall be instrumented so that torque can be determined during development, acceptance, and qualification testing.

name: Deployable Position Indication Requirements
text: Deployables shall, where practicable, have stowed and deployed position switches to indicate both release of the deployable from its restraining mechanism and end of travel or latching position. Potentiometers may be used to provide data on intermediate positions.

name: Switch Mounting and Orientation Requirements
text: Where switches are used as indicating devices for deployables, the design of the switch mounting and the switch orientation shall be such that maladjustment of the switch shall not prevent full travel of the deployable to its deployment stop.

name: Switch Actuation Direction Requirements
text: In no case shall the direction of actuation of a switch be the same as the direction of motion of the mechanism. Cam operated switches using ramps are preferred where the final position of the switch on the ramp is incapable of depressing the switch further than its normal operating range.

name: Switch Over-Travel and Sensitivity Requirements
text: Where switches are used, levers or other suitable devices shall be provided to decrease the sensitivity to adjustment of the switch and to ensure that sufficient over travel is provided after actuation of the switch.

name: Hermetic Sealing of Switches
text: Switches shall be hermetically sealed.

name: On-Orbit Thermal Instrumentation Requirements
text: Sufficient on-orbit instrumentation shall be provided to measure critical temperatures and to detect off-nominal thermal conditions.

name: Continuity of Test Parameter Measurements
text: Test points shall be provided to accommodate a continuity of critical test parameter measurements from component acceptance tests through subsystem tests, vehicle acceptance tests, prelaunch checkout, and on-orbit test measurements.

name: Telemetry Test Point Provision
text: Test points shall be provided, where practicable, as telemetry points on connector pins.

name: Selection of Test Parameters
text: The test parameters shall be chosen to provide assurance of satisfactory equipment performance and to isolate faults should they occur.

name: Parameter Test Limit Accuracy Requirements
text: The parameter test limits shall be established such that the measurements are made to an expanding accuracy tolerance that avoids the possible rejection of equipment which has passed tests conducted at lower levels of assembly.

name: Ground Test Use of On-Orbit Instrumentation
text: The on-orbit instrumentation and measurement techniques shall be used during ground tests to provide a data base that would permit parameter traceability with respect to variations in environmental conditions.

name: Failure Modes, Effects, and Criticality Analysis Required
text: Required performance and reliability shall be ensured based upon a failure modes, effects, and criticality analysis (see 6.2.9).

name: Failure Modes to Be Considered
text: The failures to be considered shall include, but are not limited to, power outage, low voltage conditions, damper leakage, binding or excessive frictional loads, increase in friction noise, over temperature conditions, excessive temperature gradients, failure of limit switches, partial or complete deployment failure, and structural failure in the moving mechanical assembly.

name: Redundancy Consideration in Preliminary Design
text: During the preliminary design phase, an initial failure mode analysis shall consider providing redundancy in the design to achieve the required reliability.

name: Failure Modes Used for Telemetry Selection
text: Failure modes established for the moving mechanical assemblies shall be used as a basis for selecting in-flight telemetry monitoring points to be used for ground diagnostic analysis should an anomalous condition occur.

name: Avoidance of Single Point Failures
text: Single point failure modes for moving mechanical assemblies and their component parts shall be avoided, where practicable.

name: Redundant Portions Must Meet All Requirements
text: Where redundancy is provided, the redundant portion of the moving mechanical assembly shall be in accordance with all the requirements of this specification.

name: Design Requirements for Unavoidable Single Point Failures
text: Where single point failure modes are unavoidable, or their avoidance is not practicable, the contractor shall ensure a satisfactory design based on an assessment of the mishap risk, and appropriate substantiating analyses and tests.

name: Reliability Estimate for Design Life
text: An estimate of the reliability for the design life of the mechanical assembly shall be included.

name: Risk Assessment for Assembly Failure
text: An assessment of the risk involved should the moving mechanical assembly fail shall be included.

name: Penalty Assessment for Redundancy
text: An assessment of the penalty to the vehicle by incorporation of redundancy or backup modes of operation shall be included.

name: Design Assessment Factors
text: The assessment shall include consideration of complexity, safety, reliability, weight, volume, and electrical power.

name: Dynamic Analysis Ensuring Stability and Rigidity
text: Adequate servo stability margins, acceptable structural rigidity including resonant frequency and damping characteristics, and acceptable interactions with the spacecraft control system shall be ensured for each moving mechanical assembly by appropriate dynamic analysis.

name: Dynamic Loading and Transient Effects Analysis
text: The analysis shall include dynamic loading effects and any effects due to changes in mass properties, momentum balance, or transient torques during operation of the moving mechanical assembly or operation of the vehicle.

name: Design Sensitivity to Off-Nominal Parameters
text: The sensitivity of the design and operational performance to changes in various parameters shall be considered and minimized in the design.

name: Off-Nominal Parameters to Be Considered
text: These off-nominal parameters shall include, but not be limited to, such items as higher dynamic response of surrounding structure, higher and lower speed of motors, higher and lower velocities of deployables, varying duty cycles, misalignments, friction due to contamination, overload and heating of motors due to stalling, inadvertent spin up of the despun portion of dual spin vehicles, inadvertent spin-up of 3 axis controlled vehicles, higher and lower spin speeds of spinning vehicles, higher and lower nutation frequencies associated with spinning vehicles, unsymmetrical deployment of solar arrays, transient over-voltage, high and low bus voltage, power down modes, and off-nominal environmental conditions including such changes in environmental conditions as those caused by a delay in deployment of a device until a subsequent ground station contact.

name: Torque and Force Margin for Moving Assemblies
text: Moving mechanical assemblies shall be designed with the highest practicable torque margin or, for linear devices, the highest practicable force margin.

name: Static and Kinetic Margin Components
text: Two components of margin shall be considered: (a) the static torque or force margin which applies to the torque or force required to overcome drive resistance, and (b) the kinetic margin which applies to the torque or force required to impart acceleration.

name: Margin Requirements Across Deployment Range
text: Deployable devices shall have torque or force margins consistent with the requirements of Paragraphs 3.3.6.1 and 3.3.6.2 at any position of the deployment range.

name: Verification of Driving Capability and Load
text: Minimum available driving capability and maximum load determination shall be verified through an appropriate test program; each element of resistance shall be characterized in this test program.

name: Torque–Current Characterization for Motors
text: Where moving mechanical assemblies are driven by electrical motors (except stepper motors), a torque versus current relationship for each motor under minimum, maximum, and ambient thermal conditions shall be established.

name: Environmental Sensitivity and Margin Verification
text: The performance sensitivity of moving mechanical assemblies to environmental variations such as temperature, pressure, acceleration, vibration, and radiation, if appropriate, shall be evaluated and the torque or force margins verified for the most critical regions of operation.

name: Redundant Spring Margin Requirements
text: In spring driven mechanisms where redundant springs are used instead of a backup deployment mechanism, the mechanism shall have a positive torque or force margin for a one-spring-out case based on combining worst case conditions.

name: Margin Assessment for Broken Spring Conditions
text: In the event of a broken spring, the remaining system margin estimate shall include resistive forces or torques which could be generated by the broken spring.

name: Minimum Driving Capability Determination
text: Minimum available driving capability shall be determined by including the worst case combination of such items as supply voltage, temperature, motor and controller parameters, and minimum available drive torque or force, all of which act so as to minimize the drive output capability.

name: Maximum Static Resistance Determination
text: Maximum static resistance determination shall include the worst case combination of such items as static friction, alignment effects, latching forces, wire harness loads, damper drag, and variations in lubricity, including degradation or depletion of lubricant under vacuum and worst case thermal conditions.

name: Initial Minimum Acceptable Static Margin
text: To avoid operational problems and to account for uncertainties, the initial design minimum acceptable static torque or force margin, based on combining worst case conditions, shall be higher than actually required as a final value, as indicated in Table 1.

name: Minimum Kinetic Margin Requirement
text: The kinetic torque or force margin shall be greater than 25 percent, where practicable. However, it should be recognized also that excessive margin requirements may be detrimental in the design of some systems.

name: Minimum Drive Capability Basis
text: The minimum drive capability shall be based on that portion of the drive output available after overcoming the maximum friction, wire bundle, and other resistance in the system.

name: Drive System Sizing for Specified Inertia or Mass
text: The drive system shall be sized to accelerate the inertia or mass specified in the design specification.

name: Tolerance Requirements for Moving Assemblies
text: Tolerances on all parts used in moving mechanical assemblies shall be established to ensure that adequate clearances are maintained under all environmentally induced conditions, including thermally induced distortions.

name: Environmental Design Margin
text: To provide a design factor of safety or margin, the moving mechanical assemblies shall be designed to function within performance specifications when exposed to environmental levels that exceed the maximum levels predicted during its service life by the specified margins.

name: Determination of Maximum Predicted Environments
text: The maximum predicted environments shall be determined in accordance with the definitions in MIL-STD-1540.

name: Launch Environment Performance Requirement
text: The equipment shall be designed to function within performance specifications after exposure in the launch configuration to the maximum launch or other nonorbital service environments. These environments include temperature, vibration, acoustic noise, shock, acceleration, atmospheric pressure, humidity, and electrical storms with associated radiation.

name: Launch Temperature Design Requirement
text: The design shall be capable of withstanding thermal environments during launch preparations and launch which are between 10 deg C (18 deg F) above the maximum predicted temperature and 10 deg C (18 deg F) below the minimum predicted temperature.

name: Random Vibration Design Margin
text: A random vibration environment that is 6 decibels (dB) above the maximum predicted levels shall be used to provide the required design margin of safety.

name: Vibration Exposure Duration Requirement
text: This design environment shall be considered to persist for three times the exposure duration associated with environmental amplitudes that are greater than one half the maximum predicted environmental amplitudes, but for not less than three minutes, along each of the three orthogonal axes.

name: Acoustic Environment Substitution Requirement
text: An acoustic design environment that is 6 dB above the maximum predicted levels shall be used instead of the mechanical vibration environment for components where mechanical vibration would not simulate imposition of the service environment.

name: Sinusoidal Vibration Design Margin
text: In cases where higher frequency sinusoidal vibration is present, the design levels shall be 6 dB above the maximum predicted levels in order to provide the required design margin of safety.

name: Shock Spectrum Design Requirement
text: The design shock spectrum shall be at least 6 dB over the maximum predicted pyrotechnic shock levels.

name: Acceleration Design Level Requirement
text: The design acceleration level shall be the maximum predicted level multiplied by an ultimate factor of safety that includes a 10 percent test measurement tolerance.

name: Launch Acceleration Ultimate Factors of Safety
text: The launch design acceleration ultimate factor of safety shall be at least 1.38 (1.25 + 10 percent) for unmanned vehicles and 1.54 (1.40 + 10 percent) for manned vehicles.

name: Yield Factor of Safety Requirement
text: Unless otherwise specified, the yield factor of safety shall be 1.0.

name: Positive Strength Margins Requirement
text: All yield and ultimate strength margins of safety shall be positive.

name: Cross-Axis Acceleration Requirement
text: When applicable, the cross axis design acceleration shall include the acceleration due to rotation.

name: Atmospheric Pressure Change Requirement
text: The design shall be capable of sustaining ambient pressures that change from sea level to 0.0133 pascals (1.929 × 10⁻⁶ pounds per square inch) in 3 minutes.

name: Humidity and Mildly Corrosive Environment Exposure Requirement
text: The design shall, where practicable, be capable of sustaining exposures up to 12 hours in duration to moderately humid or mildly corrosive environments while unprotected during manufacture or handling, such as possible industrial environments or sea coast fog that could be expected prior to launch.

name: On-Orbit Environmental Design Margin
text: The equipment shall be designed to function within performance specifications following or, if appropriate, during exposure to environmental levels that exceed the maximum predicted on-orbit environments by the design factor of safety or design margin. These environments include thermal, vacuum, radiation exposure, shock, random vibration, and acceleration.

name: Thermal and Vacuum Operating Range
text: The moving mechanical assemblies shall operate at any temperature within their thermal design range, at an ambient pressure less than 133 micropascals (1.93 × 10⁻⁷ psi). The thermal design range is from 10 deg C (18 deg F) above the maximum predicted temperature to 10 deg C (18 deg F) below the minimum predicted temperature.

name: Minimum Thermal Design Range Requirement
text: In addition, the thermal design range shall not be less than from +71 deg C to -34 deg C (160 deg F to -29 deg F) unless attainment of this capability would not be practicable or would adversely influence the design, such as necessitating the use of a less desirable lubricant.

name: Radiation Exposure Performance Requirement
text: The moving mechanical assemblies shall be designed to operate within performance specifications after exposure to on-orbit level radiation environments for the service life of the assembly.

name: Radiation Timeline Design Margin
text: The timeline of the on-orbit levels shall include a representative number of time periods at the maximum predicted radiation levels to ensure a satisfactory design margin.

name: On-Orbit Shock Spectrum Requirement
text: The design level pyrotechnic shock spectrum shall be at least 6 dB over the maximum predicted levels occurring during on-orbit operation.

name: On-Orbit Random Vibration Design Level
text: The on-orbit random vibration design level shall be at least 6 dB above the maximum predicted on-orbit levels.

name: On-Orbit Acceleration Design Level
text: The on-orbit acceleration design level shall be the maximum predicted on-orbit levels multiplied by a factor of safety that includes a 10 percent test measurement tolerance.

name: Minimum On-Orbit Acceleration Factor of Safety
text: The on-orbit design acceleration factor of safety shall be at least two.

name: Acceleration Due to Vehicle Rotation
text: When applicable, the acceleration shall include that which is due to vehicle rotation.
